races.name: fakenhamdogfield.co.uk Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Madajovy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with class credentials from Skelton yard, 20 days since disappointing effort, needs tactical race to show former ability
runners_data.comment: Placed in 2m3f/3m1f handicaps but left Dan Skelton for £4,500 and as a nine-race maiden
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up twice for Dan Skelton in the winter (2m3f/3m1f) but left that stable after a disappointing run in March and was pulled up after performing poorly for new yard three weeks ago (2m3f); back up in trip with cheekpieces refitted.

runners_data.name: Popa Rich
runners_data.note: Hold-up type suited to left-handed tracks like Fakenham having placed twice at Cartmel, 18 days since pulled-up effort at Perth
runners_data.comment: Staying-on fifth over C&D (added tongue-tie) last September; this is his first run since.
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up at Perth this month, after a layoff, but was placed twice on the tight left-handed track at Cartmel (2m6f) last summer, so there's a good chance Fakenham will also suit him; big player if back on song.

runners_data.name: Tuba
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to hurdles after AW wins, 190 days off but recent flat form suggests fitness, will control tempo with no pace pressure
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles, having been pulled up in both handicaps last year (2m1f/2m3f), but returns to this code after two 1m6f AW wins this spring and is evidenty in good nick; tries a new trip; likely contender.

runners_data.name: Dame In Disguise
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with minimal experience, pulled up last time after stumbling, wears first-time cheekpieces for improvement
runners_data.comment: Very modest form in bumpers and over hurdles, and she's held by Silvereen
runners_data.spotlight: Showed nothing more than glimmers of promise in her three qualifying races (2m-2m4f), albeit she had an excuse when pulled up last time (stumbled and lost action); makes handicap debut in a weak race, though, and the new trip may enable improvement.

runners_data.name: The Kings Soldier
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who stayed on well at Stratford over longer trip, 29 days since last run, needs strong pace to aim at
runners_data.comment: Showed much more when fourth of nine finishers up in trip at Stratford 13 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Made fairly encouraging handicap debut when keeping-on fourth at Stratford (3m2f, good) last month but was soundly beaten at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good) four weeks ago and it's hard to know what to expect from him here; 2lb out of the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Tuba will lead or go prominent early with no natural front-runners to pressure him, creating a moderate gallop over this staying trip. The four hold-up horses (Madajovy, Popa Rich, Dame In Disguise, The Kings Soldier) will track behind in a bunched field. This sets up a tactical finish where the pace-setters can dictate terms without being harried. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed, as the lack of early pressure allows Tuba to control the tempo and kick when ready.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tuba Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Tuba gets an uncontested lead and dictates a modest tempo
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows him to save energy for a sustained finish, capitalizing on his recent AW wins showing current form. His prominent style perfectly suits the tactical nature this will become.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly sedate and multiple hold-up horses get into contention late
scenarios.body: Madajovy's class edge from his Skelton days could prove decisive in a finish where stamina and finishing kick matter most. The tactical finish would suit his patient style despite recent disappointments.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Tuba goes too slow early and the race becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes about who has the most instant acceleration rather than sustained galloping, potentially suiting horses with undiscovered finishing gears. This compressed finish could level the playing field significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If genuine pace develops despite expectations and the trip becomes a true staying test
scenarios.body: The 2m7½f distance combined with good going creates a stamina examination that could expose some of these moderate handicappers. Previous course experience and proven stamina become crucial factors.

watchPoints.text: Tuba could steal this if allowed to dictate his own fractions without any pace pressure from the start
Madajovy's stable switch after poor form - watch for any signs of a training revival or continued regression
Popa Rich's course suitability given his Cartmel placings on similar left-handed configuration
Dame In Disguise wearing first-time cheekpieces which could spark significant improvement from limited exposed form
The Kings Soldier's stamina credentials tested stepping back down from 3m2f to 2m7½f

races.name: Bruce Towers & Sons Mechanical Engineers Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Baileys Big Image
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but serious fitness concerns after 266 days off and previous form suggests she fades badly in the finish
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off when 100-1 for good-ground Fontwell bumper on rules debut in September; not seen since.

runners_data.name: Skye Glance
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who should get an easy lead and showed improved form last time, making her dangerous if allowed to dictate
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to connections' smart jumper Millers Bank; beaten under 6l and appeared to display improvement when fifth of seven in good-ground Plumpton bumper last month but the value of that form is open to question; makes hurdle debut here; others look much stronger.

runners_data.name: Never Told Me
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid maiden hurdle form last summer, benefits from Fergal O'Brien's 20% strike-rate over 14 days
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed clear promise in three good-ground maiden hurdles last summer, perhaps most notably when second of five at Newton Abbot (2m1f) on latest appearance; had wind op in September and should have more to offer this year; hood removed after one use.

runners_data.name: Dancing Dame
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who showed significant improvement when sixth at Naas last time despite poor overall record
runners_data.comment: Minor ability in bumpers, modest form over hurdles so far, may do better in handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 in bumpers and 0-4 over hurdles when based in Ireland but belied 200-1 odds when very respectable sixth of 19 in good-quality Naas maiden (2m, soft to heavy) on latest outing in December; should be okay on the much quicker ground here and new stable tends to do well with new recruits.

runners_data.name: Alibey
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with strong recent form in handicaps, drops back to maiden company with 6lb claim from Worsley
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on both starts since handicapping and she's likely to be in the mix again.
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in three 2m handicaps this spring (good/good to firm), twice at Plumpton and once at Huntingdon; that form isn't anything to go wild about and her tendency to race too freely remains a nagging concern but she has another big role to play here.

races.paceDynamic: Skye Glance will take them along at a steady gallop from the front, with Never Told Me and Alibey settling prominently behind her. The small field and lack of natural pace-pressers means this will develop into a tactical affair with the tempo building gradually through the race. Dancing Dame and Baileys Big Image will be held up at the rear, relying on late kicks. This moderate early pace strongly favours hold-up horses and strong finishers who can produce their best work late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace stays steady and the race develops into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The patient tactics pay dividends as the front-runners tire and those with fresh legs can unleash devastating late runs. Dancing Dame and Never Told Me benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Skye Glance gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear at the right moment
scenarios.body: Her unopposed advantage up front allows her to dictate terms completely and she has enough left to repel late challenges. The patient hold-up horses leave their runs too late on this occasion.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Never Told Me or Alibey track the pace perfectly and time their challenges to perfection
scenarios.body: Their prominent positions allow them to respond immediately when the pace quickens, getting first run on the hold-up horses. This tactical positioning proves the winning formula between the pace extremes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely crawling and turns into a complete lottery
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure stamina test with horses stopping quickly when the sprint develops. The winner comes from whichever horse finds the most late momentum in a slowly-run affair.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Skye Glance gets an uncontested lead early - she could prove very hard to peg back if allowed to dictate completely
Monitor Dancing Dame's jumping on hurdles debut for this yard - any early mistakes could ruin her hold-up chances
Check if Never Told Me travels well in the early stages given the 274-day absence since her last promising run
Watch for any market moves on Baileys Big Image despite the long absence - yard may know more about her fitness
Observe how aggressively Alibey's 7lb claimer rides - inexperience could cost in a tactical finish

races.name: Book Your Function @fakenhamracecourse.co.uk Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Not For Passin
runners_data.note: The natural leader returns from 39 days off but faces no early pace pressure in this small field, allowing him to dictate ideal fractions.
runners_data.comment: Still early days over hurdles but he needs major improvement after a break; equipment on
runners_data.spotlight: Second in a point before readily made all in good-ground Perth bumper for an Irish stable last spring; made underwhelming start to hurdling career for new stable last season, with best of three runs his well-held second at Catterick (1m7f, good) in January, but switches to fences for this handicap debut and has plenty of scope for improvement.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner last year who excels on good ground but returns from a 166-day break that raises fitness questions.
runners_data.comment: 11yo who has been well beaten on last two starts and is 5lb out of the handicap
runners_data.spotlight: Four chase wins, the latest off today's mark in this race a year ago (good ground); absent since some below-par efforts on slower-than-ideal ground towards end of 2025 and not getting any younger but booking of Sean Bowen drops strong hint he'll be primed for a bold defence.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was well beaten at Taunton last time and faces a significant class rise after modest hurdles form.
runners_data.comment: Yet to fire over hurdles and returns from a 184-day break with something to prove.
runners_data.spotlight: Won a low-grade Flat handicap last summer but has modest record over hurdles and was well beaten at Taunton (2m, good) last month, after a layoff; might be aided by refitted cheekpieces on this chasing debut but is not bred for fences; risky.

runners_data.name: Chateau Du Lys
runners_data.note: Winless over fences but showed improved form in cheekpieces last time, though needs to find more to compete at this level.
runners_data.comment: Only third best on merit when battling on for modest second last month; more needed here
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 over fences; seemed to respond well to first-time cheekpieces when second at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) last month but was only third best on merit there and was tailed off on his latest outing; 1lb wrong here.

races.paceDynamic: Not For Passin will lead from the start without any other natural pace horses to pressure him through the early stages. The lone front runner can dictate comfortable fractions over this 2m½f trip, with Getaway Jewel, Most Wanted and Chateau Du Lys all content to track from mid-division or further back in this small field. The lack of early pace allows Not For Passin to conserve energy for a sustained gallop home, while the hold-up horses face the challenge of making up ground against a horse who hasn't been softened up. This race shape strongly favours the leader and any prominent racers who can stay close enough to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Not For Passin jumps cleanly and maintains his rhythm without early pressure
scenarios.body: The front runner can dictate ideal fractions and prove difficult to peg back over this longer trip. His fresh reappearance and the lack of early pace pressure creates perfect conditions for a pillar-to-post victory.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Comeback Success
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders go too steady early and one of the hold-up horses finds extra gear
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace creates a falsely-run race that sets up perfectly for a closer with tactical speed. Getaway Jewel's course and distance form makes her the most likely beneficiary of this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If Not For Passin makes a crucial mistake at a key fence under pressure
scenarios.body: A mistake from the leader opens the door for the patient rides to capitalise in the closing stages. The relatively inexperienced chasers in this field make jumping errors a realistic possibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Not For Passin goes faster than ideal early trying to put distance on his rivals
scenarios.body: The increased pace could find out the stamina reserves of some runners over this extended trip. Most Wanted's modest recent form makes him vulnerable if the race becomes a true test of staying power.

watchPoints.text: Not For Passin's jumping fluency in the home straight as any mistake could let in the closers
Getaway Jewel's early position as she needs to be close enough to strike despite her hold-up style
Most Wanted's response to pressure as his recent Taunton effort suggests he may struggle at this level
The early pace tempo as a falsely-run race could set up the hold-up horses perfectly
Chateau Du Lys maintains her improved attitude with the cheekpieces retained from her better recent effort

races.name: 1st The Queens' Dragoon Guards Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ambiente Friendly
runners_data.note: Free-going hold-up horse whose tendency to race keenly could be problematic behind Hello Sweety's likely strong pace
runners_data.comment: Broadly too free for his own good since switched to hurdles; needs to settle better
runners_data.spotlight: Smart 3yo on the Flat; just 1-5 over hurdles, and his habit of racing far too freely remains a worry, but he wasn't beaten far in a valuable novices' handicap at Sandown (2m, good) last month and is in much calmer waters here.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Proven over the distance with good going form, the 241-day break is a concern but trainer Jack Jones strikes at 13% with returning horses
runners_data.comment: Won Chelmsford handicap in November; off since but yard going well so not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice over hurdles (2m/2m4f, good) and twice on the Flat in 2025; looked as good as ever when second on the Flat this month, after a break, and is respected, albeit the nagging concern is that he ran poorly on his only previous visit to Fakenham.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: New yard debut for Neil King who strikes at 25% with new recruits, the visor replacement with tongue-tie suggests tactical changes
runners_data.spotlight: Twice made the frame at Sedgefield (2m1f, good) for Brian Ellison last month; left that yard after a disappointing Flat run but was in contention before awkward jumps at last two flights proved costly on recent stable debut at Newton Abbot (2m2f, good); swaps usual cheekpices for first-time visor; can make her presence felt.

runners_data.name: Hello Sweety
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 57-day break with trainer Stuart Edmunds hitting 0/4 in the last 14 days, needs to settle better than usual
runners_data.comment: Dual hurdles winner over the winter; lightly raced and can make her presence felt
runners_data.spotlight: Free-going front-runner who won twice over C&D last season (soft/good to soft), both times by wide margins in modest mares' races; probably went off too hard when well beaten at Huntingdon last month but steadied the ship with respectable Flat run 24 days ago; sure to be suited by return to this track but stiil needs to prove she can cope with a mark this high.

races.paceDynamic: Hello Sweety will take the field along from the front as the only confirmed leader, but with just four runners this won't create a particularly strong gallop. The three hold-up horses - Ambiente Friendly, An Bradan Feasa, and Blackwater Lilly - will all be tracking behind, likely bunched together in the small field. With Hello Sweety's free-going nature potentially seeing her go too hard early, this sets up a tactical affair where the patient hold-up horses can time their challenges. This race shape clearly favours the prominent trackers and hold-up horses who can exploit Hello Sweety's front-running tactics over 2m.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hello Sweety Burns Out
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Sweety goes too hard early and fades from the last hurdle
scenarios.body: Her front-running style over-commits in the small field, leaving the door open for the hold-up brigade to sweep past. The patient tactics of the tracking trio prove decisive as they pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Sweety can restrain her natural eagerness and dictate sensibly
scenarios.body: She uses the lack of pace pressure to her advantage, controlling the tempo throughout before finding extra when challenged. The hold-up horses struggle to make up ground against her sustained effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too slow for Hello Sweety's kick and one tracker times it perfectly
scenarios.body: The modest early gallop sets up a sprint finish where class tells over the final furlong. An Bradan Feasa or Ambiente Friendly use their superior ratings to devastating effect.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blackwater Lilly Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the yard change has freshened her up and she gets a perfect run
scenarios.body: Neil King's new recruit benefits from the tactical race shape, finding gaps as the others commit too early. Her recent Sedgefield form proves more relevant than her poor last run.

watchPoints.text: Hello Sweety's early position - if she's allowed an uncontested lead she could prove hard to peg back despite her free-going nature
An Bradan Feasa's jumping after the long break - any early mistakes could prove costly in a small field where positions are crucial
Ambiente Friendly's settling - his tendency to race too freely could see him use up vital energy tracking Hello Sweety's likely strong gallop
Blackwater Lilly's market move - any significant support would suggest the yard change has worked wonders
The pace through the first mile - if Hello Sweety goes too fast early, it sets up the hold-up horses perfectly

races.name: Prince Of Wales Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Coastguard Station
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning to a course where he won in 2024, but faces a genuine pace that may not suit his style with 16 days since Aintree fourth.
runners_data.comment: Enjoys good ground; bumped into the enigmatic Numitor on a good day at Hereford last month
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground specialist who was a course winner in 2024 and returns here after two good efforts this spring, the latter a close fourth at Aintree (2m4f, good) 16 days ago; respected.

runners_data.name: Nickelforce
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can track the early pace and has tactical speed, with Harry Bannister taking over and 29 days since respectable Uttoxeter third.
runners_data.spotlight: 3-14 over fences, the latest win gained at Wincanton (2m4f, good) in November; just a respectable third at Uttoxeter (2m5f, good) this month, his second start after a layoff, and remains on fairly tough mark but still enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in excellent form after Huntingdon win, wearing first-time tongue tie and reunited with Tom Cannon after 24-day break.
runners_data.comment: Ran well for a long way over 3m last time but has been well below his best for a while now
runners_data.spotlight: Well below best last season but exploited some help from the handicapper when winning in pretty good style at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) this month; even after a 5lb rise, he's still 5lb lower than when winning this race in 2025; good chance.

runners_data.name: No But I Will
runners_data.note: Another front-runner with course-winning form but 47 days off and jockey taking 7lb claim, making the early pace battle crucial to his chances.
runners_data.comment: Won on stable debut in December and also ran well when reappearing last month; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Just held on to make winning stable debut over C&D (soft) in December but failed to build upon an encouraging reappearance run when tailed off at Market Rasen last month; others have more persuasive profiles.

runners_data.name: Tommy Cullen
runners_data.note: Prominent type on attractive mark after two modest fourths, with Jack Quinlan able to position him tactically behind the early leaders.
runners_data.comment: Seems best at Doncaster but on a fair mark and he's able when fresh
runners_data.spotlight: Hit prolonged flat spots before keeping on for modest fourth over 2m on latest two appearances, the latest at Warwick this month; on a good mark now and this step back up in trip could be the right move but it remains to be seen whether Jack Quinlan can keep him in touch this time.

races.paceDynamic: Hurricane Bay and No But I Will will set a genuine pace from the start, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead over the first mile. The honest gallop will stretch the small field, particularly as Hurricane Bay showed good pace at Huntingdon and No But I Will has front-running form at this course. Coastguard Station and the other hold-up horses will need the leaders to maintain their tempo to set up a finishing kick. This shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed to track the pace, as the small field and genuine early gallop will make it difficult for hold-up horses to make up significant ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Favours Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Hurricane Bay and No But I Will maintain honest fractions without killing each other
scenarios.body: The tempo stays strong but not suicidal, allowing the front pair to stay competitive while stretching the field behind. Hurricane Bay's recent Huntingdon form and No But I Will's course-winning experience give them the edge over closers who may struggle to make up ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stop-start or one leader drops away early
scenarios.body: The race develops into a sprint finish where horses with tactical pace and good positioning prove decisive. Nickelforce and Tommy Cullen can track the pace and have the speed to quicken, while pure hold-up horses get caught flat-footed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Sets Up Closer
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast and tire dramatically in the straight
scenarios.body: The honest early gallop becomes unsustainable, creating perfect conditions for Coastguard Station to use his proven finishing kick. His good ground form and recent Aintree fourth show he has the class to capitalise when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Front Runner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Tommy Cullen or Nickelforce go forward to avoid the early battle
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners decides to make early use and avoids getting caught behind a fierce pace battle. This tactical switch allows them to control the race and kick clear when the recognised leaders engage in their duel.

watchPoints.text: Hurricane Bay and No But I Will engage in a pace duel that's too fierce and both tire dramatically in the straight
Coastguard Station gets too far back early if the pace is genuinely strong, making his finishing kick ineffective
Tommy Cullen's positioning in the first half-mile as he could benefit from tracking rather than making the running
No But I Will's jumping early on after 47 days off and with an inexperienced jockey taking a 7lb claim
Nickelforce's ability to handle the step up in trip from his recent 2m4f efforts to this 2m5f contest

races.name: Fisher Electrical Contractors Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Pro Jockeys/Amateur Riders')

runners_data.name: Market House
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won last time out wearing a visor for the first time but racing without headgear today, with consistent form on good ground this year.
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent on the Flat/over hurdles this year, and deserved last month's narrow win at Plumpton (2m, good; only time he wore a visor); can remain very competitive after 3lb rise.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from wind operation with 17 days since last run, needing a strong pace to be effective but getting 5lb claim from Ryder.
runners_data.comment: Five-time runner-up over fences; wind surgery followed heavy hurdles defeat in November
runners_data.spotlight: Safely held when fourth over fences at Fontwell (2m2f, good) this month but that was his first run since November (also his first after a wind op); reverts to hurdling on mark just 2lb higher then when winning this race by 14l on good ground a year ago; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Nottodaybobo
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner wearing a tongue-tie who has found form for new stable, perfectly positioned to control this small field from the lead.
runners_data.comment: Ended 2025 in poor form but his keeping-on third at Newcastle in March was much better
runners_data.spotlight: Has turned a corner since returning from a break this spring and came good for current stable with front-running win at Market Rasen (2m4f, good) three weeks ago; that form looks modest but he ought to give another good account here.

runners_data.name: Winston's Oath
runners_data.note: Prominent 4yo with limited hurdling experience but showed promise when third over course and distance last time, representing the least exposed option.
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who displayed significant promise when third of six against own age-group over C&D (good) last month; well beaten on both hurdling starts either side of that but his course form brings him into the equation on this handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: Nottodaybobo will set the pace from the front with her confirmed leading style, likely getting an uncontested lead given the small field and lack of other natural pace-setters. Market House and Winston's Oath will sit prominently behind the leader, while Gone In Sixty will be held up at the rear by Ryder. The modest pace will allow Nottodaybobo to dictate terms and kick for home when ready, while the prominent runners can stay in touch without pressure. This tactical setup strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can track the pace and strike, rather than hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nottodaybobo Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Nottodaybobo gets an easy lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: She can use her recent front-running win at Market Rasen as a blueprint, controlling the race from pillar to post. The lack of early pace pressure allows her to save energy for a decisive move that the prominent runners struggle to match.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Market House or Winston's Oath can track Nottodaybobo and produce superior finishing speed
scenarios.body: The consistent Market House or improving Winston's Oath can sit second/third, let Nottodaybobo do the donkey work, then sweep past in the final furlong. Their prominent styles are perfectly suited to this patient tracking role.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Gone In Sixty Surprise Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly pedestrian and Gone In Sixty gets a perfect ride from the back
scenarios.body: Ryder can use her claim effectively and time a late challenge from the rear as others tie up. The hold-up style works only if the early pace is crawling and she has enough petrol left after her wind operation.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Winston's Oath Age Advantage
scenarios.trigger: If the 4yo's class and potential progression kicks in during the race
scenarios.body: His third place over course and distance last time suggests he's learning the game, and his younger legs could prove decisive in a finish between tired rivals. The unexposed element gives him an edge if finding improvement.

watchPoints.text: Gone In Sixty needs a strong early pace to be competitive but Nottodaybobo's uncontested lead could leave her with too much ground to make up.
Market House raced in a visor when winning last time but goes without headgear today, potentially affecting his focus and determination.
Winston's Oath has the smallest sample size over hurdles but his third place here last month suggests the track suits his style.
Nottodaybobo's tongue-tie could slip or cause discomfort during the race, potentially affecting her jumping rhythm.
The 5lb claim for Isabelle Ryder on Gone In Sixty becomes crucial if the finish is tight between the lower-weighted runners.
